Test transitions against no sequential structure by permutation

Source: R/permute_lsa.R
permute_lsa.Rd

permute_lsa() tests every transition of a fit from lsa() against no sequential structure by permutation: whether the transition is over- or under-represented beyond what the same events in a random order would give, keeping the frequency of every state fixed. The adjusted residual of a transition is otherwise tested against a normal reference distribution, which holds only approximately, for large counts and independent transitions. A permutation test builds the reference distribution from the data instead: if the order of events carried no information, shuffling the events would produce residuals as large as the observed ones.

The events of the fit are shuffled many times, by default within each sequence so that every sequence keeps its own length and state frequencies; the model is refitted with the same engine and settings, and the adjusted residual of every transition is recorded. The two-sided permutation p-value of a transition is the share of shuffles whose residual is at least as large in absolute value as the observed one, counted so that it is never zero (Phipson & Smyth, 2010). A transition is significant when its p-value is below the alpha of the fit.

The p-values are not corrected for the number of transitions tested. For intervals on the residuals and other statistics, use bootstrap_lsa(); for the share of subsamples in which a transition stays significant, use stability_lsa(). To test whether groups differ, use compare_lsa().

Usage

permute_lsa(
  fit,
  R = 1000L,
  within_sequence = TRUE,
  shuffles = NULL,
  parallel = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

An lsa fit from lsa(), built from sequences (not from a transition matrix).

R

Number of permutations. Default 1000.

within_sequence

Shuffle events within each sequence (TRUE, default) or across the whole event stream (FALSE). A single sequence is always shuffled as a whole, with a warning when within_sequence = TRUE.

shuffles

Optional list of at least R permutations of seq_len(n_events) to replay instead of random shuffles. Default NULL.

parallel

Run the permutations on several cores. Default FALSE.

n_cores

Number of cores when parallel = TRUE. Default NULL, all cores but one.

verbose

Report progress every 100 permutations. Default FALSE.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class c("lsa_permutation", "list"). Read it with transitions(), which returns a data frame with one row per transition (from -> to pair) and the columns from, to, observed_count, observed_adj_res, p_perm (permutation p-value; NA for transitions that cannot be estimated, such as structural zeros) and significant (p_perm below the fit's alpha). transitions(x, significant = TRUE) keeps the significant transitions; sort = "strength" orders by the absolute observed residual. print() shows the settings and the number of significant transitions (see lsa-inference-methods). The object also stores the permuted residuals, the settings and the original fit.

Conditions

Errors carry the class lagdynamics_error and one of:

  • lagdynamics_needs_events: the fit was built from a transition matrix, so there are no events to shuffle.

  • lagdynamics_bad_input: shuffles is not a list of at least R permutations of seq_len(n_events).

References

Castellan, N. J. (1992). Shuffling arrays: Appearances may be deceiving. Behavior Research Methods, Instruments, & Computers, 24(1), 72-77.

Phipson, B., & Smyth, G. K. (2010). Permutation p-values should never be zero: Calculating exact p-values when permutations are randomly drawn. Statistical Applications in Genetics and Molecular Biology, 9(1), Article 39.

See also

transitions() to read the result; bootstrap_lsa(), stability_lsa() and reliability_lsa() for other checks of a fit; compare_lsa() to compare groups.

Examples

fit <- lsa(engagement)
pm <- permute_lsa(fit, R = 100)
pm
#> <lsa_permutation>
#>   engine:        classical
#>   replicates:    100
#>   within seq:    TRUE
#>   significant edges (p_perm < 0.050): 7 of 9
transitions(pm, significant = TRUE, sort = "strength")
#>         from         to observed_count observed_adj_res     p_perm significant
#> 1     Active     Active            459        21.662811 0.00990099        TRUE
#> 2 Disengaged Disengaged            157        15.390466 0.00990099        TRUE
#> 3    Average     Active            153       -12.906038 0.00990099        TRUE
#> 4     Active Disengaged             23       -12.556925 0.00990099        TRUE
#> 5    Average    Average            458        12.452615 0.00990099        TRUE
#> 6     Active    Average            176       -11.319132 0.02970297        TRUE
#> 7 Disengaged    Average            129        -1.736461 0.00990099        TRUE
# \donttest{
# A full analysis uses more permutations
permute_lsa(fit, R = 1000) |>
  transitions(sort = "strength")
#>         from         to observed_count observed_adj_res      p_perm significant
#> 1     Active     Active            459       21.6628107 0.000999001        TRUE
#> 2 Disengaged Disengaged            157       15.3904661 0.000999001        TRUE
#> 3    Average     Active            153      -12.9060384 0.000999001        TRUE
#> 4     Active Disengaged             23      -12.5569254 0.000999001        TRUE
#> 5    Average    Average            458       12.4526148 0.000999001        TRUE
#> 6     Active    Average            176      -11.3191319 0.006993007        TRUE
#> 7 Disengaged     Active             39      -10.5494860 0.068931069       FALSE
#> 8 Disengaged    Average            129       -1.7364613 0.022977023        TRUE
#> 9    Average Disengaged            140        0.1757996 0.828171828       FALSE
# }
